## What you should be able to do tonight

- State how many free parameters a mean-variance problem on N assets requires, and how that grows.
- Reproduce the estimation-error argument against raw optimisation from memory, with a number attached.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>35 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Finish anything outstanding from days 99 to 104. The rolling out-of-sample horse race is the piece worth having complete, because week 16 measures improvements against it.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [15 min]{.task-min} Count the parameters, closed book: N means, N variances and N choose 2 correlations, evaluated at N of 25, 100 and 500, against the number of monthly observations you have. Then write the sentence that follows from the comparison.

## Drill <span class='task-total'>interview thread</span>

Spaced repetition, not cramming. Every drill in the year is collected on the [drills page](../drills.qmd).

::: {.task-list .drill}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Arithmetic, timed, fifteenth sitting. Ten two-digit multiplications, the sevenths, and 1.02 to the 36th power approximated in your head.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Random walk, first passage: a symmetric random walk starts at 0. What is the probability it ever reaches plus 5? Now what is the expected time to do so? Say the second answer out loud before you compute it, and notice that it is surprising.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> Optional stopping, gently: you flip a fair coin and win one unit for heads, lose one for tails. You stop when you are up 1 unit. Is this a winning strategy? Say precisely which assumption of optional stopping fails, and what a broker would call the thing that makes it fail.
:::
:::
